newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols edge up on Buba statement.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols edge up on Buba statement.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options edged higher at midday Wednesday when the spot jumped after the Bundesbank criticized German government plans to revalue the central bank's gold and currency reserves.

The dollar raced from below 1.6900 marks to above 1.7050 after the Bundesbank issued a statement saying the plan was an intrusion into Bundesbank independence and any payout of valuation gains risked undermining confidence in European Monetary Union.
"It created some volatility that has caused offers to move back a little," said an options dealer in New York.
One-month dollar/mark volatility was 9.5/9.7 percent at midday, up about 0.1 point from early U.S. levels, and one-year also rose about 0.1 point to 9.35/9.50 percent.

However, those values were off slightly from levels seen Tuesday on a push above 1.70 marks tied to fresh worries over European monetary union after the French left's legislative win in first-round elections.

Spot dollar/mark has since backed off and was last trading at 1.6950 marks. The mark initially garnered support this morning from the view that a Socialist win in the second round of French elections could hamper EMU.

On Tuesday, the prospect of a Socialist victory in France had raised fears of soft euro and soft mark and bolstered the dollar against the mark, analysts said. They noted one-month 25-delta dollar/mark risk reversals were trading around par, shifting from a slight mark call bias Tuesday.
Dollar/yen volatilities slipped 0.1 point on the day, to 11.4/11.7 percent for one-month options and 10.3/10.5 percent for the one-year.
But analysts said the market remained jittery about the potential for another break in the spot, and that was keeping volatility levels underpinned.
"People are still scared about dollar/yen," said an options dealer for a U.S. brokerage house.
However, demand for options has slowed since last week's drop in the dollar below 112.00 yen, traders and analysts said. Recently, the spot was trading around 115.80 yen.
As dollar/yen has stabilized, the spread between one-month dollar/yen and dollar/mark volatilities has narrowed back to 2.0 points after expanding as wide as 4.0 points last week, analysts noted.
One-month 25-delta risk reversals remained skewed to yen calls at 1.0/1.3 but had narrowed slightly from the previous sesson.
